  b9d9e bootflow cmdline [set|get|clear|delete|auto] <param> [<value>] - update cmdline
  b9dee [addr [initrd[:size]] [fdt]]
  b9e0b     - boot Linux flat or compressed 'Image' stored at 'addr'
  b9e48 	The argument 'initrd' is optional and specifies the address
  b9e85 	of an initrd in memory. The optional parameter ':size' allows
  b9ec4 	specifying the size of a RAW initrd.
  b9eea 	Currently only booting from gz, bz2, lzma and lz4 compression
  b9f29 	types are supported. In order to boot from any of these compressed
  b9f6d 	images, user have to set kernel_comp_addr_r and kernel_comp_size environment
  b9fbb 	variables beforehand.
  b9fd2 	Since booting a Linux kernel requires a flat device-tree, a
  ba00f 	third argument providing the address of the device-tree blob
  ba04d 	is required. To boot a kernel with a device-tree blob but
  ba088 	without an initrd image, use a '-' for the initrd argument.
  ba0c6 [addr [arg ...]]
  ba0d7     - boot application image stored in memory
  ba105 	passing arguments 'arg ...'; when booting a Linux kernel,
  ba140 	'arg' can be the address of an initrd image
  ba16d 	When booting a Linux kernel which requires a flat device-tree
  ba1ac 	a third argument is required which is the address of the
  ba1e6 	device-tree blob. To boot that kernel without an initrd image,
  ba226 	use a '-' for the second argument. If you do not pass a third
  ba265 	a bd_info struct will be passed instead
  ba290 For the new multi component uImage format (FIT) addresses
  ba2ca 	must be extended to include component or configuration unit name:
  ba30d 	addr:<subimg_uname> - direct component image specification

 5a4233     - boot Linux flat or compressed 'Image' stored at 'addr'

 5a42ec 	specifying the size of a RAW initrd.
 5a4312 	Currently only booting from gz, bz2, lzma and lz4 compression
 5a4351 	types are supported. In order to boot from any of these compressed
 5a4395 	images, user have to set kernel_comp_addr_r and kernel_comp_size environment
 5a43e3 	variables beforehand.
 5a43fa 	Since booting a Linux kernel requires a flat device-tree, a
 5a4437 	third argument providing the address of the device-tree blob
 5a4475 	is required. To boot a kernel with a device-tree blob but
 5a44b0 	without an initrd image, use a '-' for the initrd argument.
 5a44ee [addr [arg ...]]
 5a44ff     - boot application image stored in memory
 5a452d 	passing arguments 'arg ...'; when booting a Linux kernel,
 5a4568 	'arg' can be the address of an initrd image
 5a4595 	When booting a Linux kernel which requires a flat device-tree
 5a45d4 	a third argument is required which is the address of the
 5a460e 	device-tree blob. To boot that kernel without an initrd image,
 5a464e 	use a '-' for the second argument. If you do not pass a third
 5a468d 	a bd_info struct will be passed instead
